1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height, though letter spacing looks default rather than deliberately generous.

2.why: Instructions are short sentence-case paragraphs with no italics, no all-caps text, and no dense blocks anywhere in the screenshots.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text and full-width buttons, which remains readable and well organised at mobile width.

4.why: Each screen gives only one or two plain-language sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone. The code expires in 10 minutes.'

5.why: Only the phone field shows an example placeholder (+447700900000); the email and verification-code fields display no example of the expected input format.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than two short sentences to proceed, and the Logs card text is likewise brief.

7.why: The six-digit code must be transcribed by hand from the SMS; no code or secret is ever presented in a copyable form in the observed steps.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears in any of the five provided screenshots.

9.why: The fields are plain text inputs with no visible autocomplete/one-time-code hints or password-manager affordances, so support cannot be confirmed beyond default browser behaviour.

10.why: The 'Step 1 of 3'/'Step 2 of 3' label plus a single high-contrast dark-blue primary button make the current step and main action stand out clearly.

11.why: Each screen asks for one primary action (Continue / Verify and continue), with only a low-emphasis 'Use different details' escape option alongside it.

12.why: After Continue the next screen plainly states a code was sent and what to enter, and after a failed attempt the banner plainly says the request failed and to try again.

13.why: The error state retains the entered code and invites 'Please try again' with no shown penalty, although no resend, reveal, or hide control is offered.

14.why: The banner 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blame but never states the actual problem, such as a wrong or expired code.

15.why: Nothing limits reading time, and the stated 10-minute validity of the code provides a generous window to enter it.
